ALL 46 "UNREAD" MONTREAL YMCA SERIALS, DOWNLOADED AND SEARCHED
Run 2026-09-07 under p_462. Every text item on that priority's unread list was
fetched in full and searched for Kanawana, Otoreke and two OCR variants.

=====================================================================
THE RESULT IN ONE LINE
=====================================================================

SIX OF THE FORTY-SIX CARRY A NAMED HIT. ALL SIX WERE ALREADY EXTRACTED.
The other forty have no occurrence of either camp's name at all.

So the text half of p_462 is finished, and it is finished as a null. That is
worth more than it sounds: it means nobody needs to open these forty again
looking for camp content, and the priority can stop listing them as an order of
attack.

=====================================================================
THE SIX, AND WHERE EACH ALREADY LIVES
=====================================================================

  the-news-bulletin-vol-15-no-01          Kanawana=1 Otoreke=1
      held as src_ia_ymca_montreal_news_bulletin_15_01
  sgw-ymca-annual-report-1959-short       Kanawana=3 Otoreke=3
      THE RICHEST OF THEM, and already read earlier the same day: the
      "Operation P. G. D." passage is f_5256, and the distinction it draws --
      that 1959 was COUNSELLOR AND STAFF TRAINING while the 1961 report's
      "second season" is about PROGRAM AND CAMP SUPERVISION -- is already
      written there. Its capital line, "Camps Kanawana, Perrot, and Otoreke
      benefited $75,000 in capital replacement and addition through the
      decade", is the one sentence in these forty-six not obviously already
      used, and it is a figure for three camps together over ten years.
  national-council-bulletin-vol-36-no-04  Kanawana=1
      "F. William Halliday, from Calgary to Ass't and Camp Kanawana,
      Montreal-North Mount" -- already at directors-index.md:504, with the two
      cautions that travel with it.
  national-council-bulletin-vol-40-no-02  Otoreke=1
  national-council-bulletin-vol-40-no-03  Otoreke=1
      "So-Ed Youth Cultural Exchange, Otoreke, Montreal, P.Q.", July 9-15 --
      already at camp-otoreke.md:734, with the right caution that a calendar
      announces rather than reports.
  bulletin-1970-02-13                     Kanawana=1
      The West Island Branch family ski programme, "It's mainly because of the
      soup" -- already at winter-programming.md:24, cited there from the
      Montreal bulletin of 29 JANUARY 1970. This item is dated 13 FEBRUARY.
      The same paragraph in two bulletins a fortnight apart is a small thing
      and not nothing: it travelled.

=====================================================================
THE WARNING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE NULL
=====================================================================

p_462'S "UNREAD" LIST IS ABOUT ONE-THIRD STALE, AND WAS WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN.
Fifteen of the forty-six are already referenced somewhere in sources.json:

  sgw-ymca-annual-report-1874 · the-news-bulletin-vol-07-no-01 ·
  ...-vol-08-no-02 · ...-vol-12-no-03 · ...-vol-15-no-01 · ...-vol-19-no-03 ·
  ...-vol-21-no-04 · ...-vol-24-no-04 · sgw-ymca-annual-report-1959-short-version ·
  national-council-bulletin-vol-36-no-04 · ...-vol-38-no-04 · ...-vol-39-no-03 ·
  ...-vol-40-no-02 · ...-vol-40-no-03 · ...-vol-41-no-03

THE MECHANISM. The enumeration decided "unread" by matching item identifiers
against what the project cites. An item read in a session that recorded it
under a source id whose text does not contain the identifier shows up as
unread. It is the same error class as a mistyped URL recorded as a dead site:
A GAP IN OUR INDEX READ AS A GAP IN THE WORLD.

THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS. An enumeration is a snapshot of our own bookkeeping, not
a to-do list. Before working any item off a list like this, GREP THE
DESTINATION -- sources.json, the KB and the wiki -- for the item and for its
distinctive contents. That check cost seconds here and would have saved a
write-up of six findings this project already had.
